facts.text: A family waits for the dial-up modem to stop screeching before opening a web page.
Using a dial-up connection can tie up the household telephone line.
More homes switch to faster internet connections that do not block telephone calls.
A home computer often sits on a desk with a separate monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
Bulky picture-tube computer monitors gradually give way to thinner flat-panel screens.
Students carry school assignments between computers on floppy disks early in the decade.
Small flash drives become a handy way to carry documents between computers.
Families burn photographs or music onto blank compact discs.
A home printer may run out of ink just before a school report is due.
An office worker checks email at a desktop computer before answering telephone messages.
A family uses a digital camera and transfers pictures to a computer.
Many families still take photographs on film early in the decade.
A camera owner plugs a memory card into a computer to sort photographs.
A portable digital music player lets a teenager carry many songs in a pocket.
People still listen to music on compact discs in cars and bedrooms.
A family rents a film on a disc and plays it in a machine beside the television.
Videotape players remain in some living rooms even as disc players become more popular.
A television set may connect to a cable box and a separate disc player.
Flat-screen televisions become more affordable and increasingly replace bulky picture-tube sets.
A child plays games on a home console using a controller connected to the television.
Some households use cordless landline phones with handsets resting in charging cradles.
Adults carry mobile phones for calls and text messages, especially later in the decade.
A teenager sends short text messages by pressing number keys several times for letters.
Early smartphones are expensive and uncommon, while most mobile phones use physical buttons.
Wireless home networks let several computers share an internet connection.
A shopper signs a receipt after a clerk swipes a payment card through a reader.
A supermarket cashier scans barcodes while the register totals the groceries.
A household uses a microwave oven to reheat leftovers in minutes.
